_note: The Remembrance page (docs/gameplay-design.md §6): observations, never tasks. Each entry is unlocked once into the quest-graph flag rem:<id> by one trigger. on: an event raised by the world (nook:<id>, talk:<npc>, cast:<surface|any>:<element|verb>, react:shatter); has: a state polled twice a second (a flag or variable, or lore:/shrine:/echo:/restored:/flow: prefixes). cell [surface, element] puts a reaction in the journal's living table; reveal [place ids] makes the places known on the compass and map.

entries.title: The Run Ends at a Fire
entries.text: The Run does not end at the camp. It ends a little short of it, on purpose: the Shapers made the pilgrims walk the last part with the fire in sight.

entries.title: The Held Snow, from Above
entries.text: Seen from the ridge it is only a hill with too many corners. The snow around it does not drift. Everything else on the steppe leans downwind; this does not.

entries.title: The Monastery from the East
entries.text: From here the roof is a line, and the fallen part is a gap in the line. Someone has been keeping the gap clear of snow.

entries.title: Where the Snow Gives Out
entries.text: The snow stops along a line you could draw with a ruler. Past it the land is brown, and then green, and nothing about the wind changes at all.

entries.title: Hearn, from the Last Turn
entries.text: Smoke goes straight up from every roof. In a place with wind it would lean. The village is built for wind that has not come in a long time.

entries.title: The Lake Holds Its Breath
entries.text: The water has no ripples from this side, none, even where the reeds are moving. Only the reeds are moving.

entries.title: Across the Water
entries.text: The far shore is dry grass and nothing else. A long way beyond it, the ground goes down and does not come up again until it is a different colour.

entries.title: The East Plain
entries.text: The grass lies one way, all of it, as if combed. It has lain that way since the wind stopped. Walk against it and you can feel the old direction.

entries.title: South of Hearn
entries.text: The road south is the same road for as far as there is to see. No one who has walked it has come back with a different opinion of it.

entries.title: Water Keeps Its Last Motion
entries.text: The Sleeping Spring is frozen mid-ripple. Ice does not do that by itself. Something stopped the water while it was still deciding.

entries.title: A Stair Built for Something Larger
entries.text: The steps are too tall for a person and too wide for a procession. Whatever climbed them climbed them often, and slowly, and was heavy.

entries.title: Nine Stones, One Shadow
entries.text: With the ninth stone up, the shadows of the nine meet in the middle at noon on the longest day, as Orm's grandfather meant them to.

entries.title: The Ground Stops
entries.text: West of the lake road the land falls away and the wind comes up the slope like a held breath let go. This is where wind went when it left.

entries.title: Rest is Remembered
entries.text: A shrine does not heal. It remembers that you stopped, and it will carry you back to any place you have stopped before. That is all rest ever was.

entries.title: Warm Stones in the Grass
entries.text: The meadow shrines are warm in all weathers. The frost ones are warm only under the frost. The stones were set to hold whatever the place was missing.

entries.title: The Shapers Left Voices
entries.text: Each Echo stone has one thing said on it, and nothing else. They were not written to be read. They were written so that whoever stood there would hear them in their own voice.

entries.title: The Bell That Fell to Ring
entries.text: The bell hangs where no foot can climb, in a frame built for a bell and not for a hand, and its clapper is a mace. Whoever hung it meant you to rise first, and to ring it on the way down.

entries.title: Hounds Hunt in Turns
entries.text: Never all at once. One breaks from the pack, the others hold; when it fails, the next one. A fight against hounds is a queue.

entries.title: The Brute Shows Its Back
entries.text: The crust along a drift brute cracks and glows a breath before it slams. It is the only warning it gives, and it gives it every time.

entries.title: The Seer Aims Where You Will Be
entries.text: A seer throws at the place you are heading, not the place you are. Stop, and the shards pass through where you were going to be.

entries.title: Old Rime Turns Blows
entries.text: The den mother has grown frost over frost for longer than the pilgrims have had songs. Only cold reaches her. Freeze her and she is only stone.

entries.title: The Grass Runs
entries.text: Sedgerunners lie in the tall grass and break all at once. They are light. A Gust will bowl one over like a dropped basket.

entries.title: The Hedge Keeps Count
entries.text: A hedgewarden keeps its boundary and ignores everything outside it. Stay out of its ring and it never turns its head; step in, and it is slow, and heavy, and certain.

entries.title: Chanters Sing the Wind Back
entries.text: A chanter stands back and sings the wounded whole. Silence it first, or the fight does not end; it was never meant to.

entries.title: Sand Moves Before It Breaks
entries.text: A mound travels against the wind. Before it leaps, sand streams away from it; cold holds the ground firm under its feet.

entries.title: The Stones Have Seams
entries.text: The plate-back wears the ruins on its back. Sand binds the seams, and ice will break them; a blow from the side finds what the stone cannot cover.

entries.title: A Heart Inside the Wind
entries.text: The sand tightens before it flies. Cold makes a pillar of the turning column; a contrary wind holds its glass heart still.

entries.title: Cold Opens the Glass
entries.text: Stone rings against the glass and falls away. Frost lays a web of pale cracks through it, and the next blow has somewhere to go.

entries.title: A Glacier That Learned to Walk
entries.text: It holds the steppe still in its water joints. The Shapers meant it to keep the snow moving. It kept the snow instead.

entries.title: Crystals First
entries.text: The pillars wake it, and the crystals on the pillars wake it more. Break the crystals, and it has to stop and gather itself. That is when to be behind stone.

entries.title: It Lay Down
entries.text: It did not die. It lay down, and the snow it had been holding went on its way. The steppe is the first thing that has moved there in a hundred winters.

entries.title: The Manor on the Hill
entries.text: The hill road runs up to the manor, and the Shaped came down it at dusk. No one in Hearn walks it after dark, and no one will say they stopped.

entries.title: The Bellwether Rests
entries.text: The Bellwether lay down. The hill road is only a road now, and Hearn has stopped looking up at the hill before it goes to sleep.

entries.title: Aud Counts the Stones
entries.text: Aud keeps the tally of everyone who took the Run and left a stone. She cannot tell you how many. She can tell you the oldest ones are under snow.

entries.title: Maren Remembers Weather
entries.text: Old Maren is the last at the fire who remembers a storm. She describes it the way other people describe a person.

entries.title: Tobin Listens at the Spring
entries.text: Tobin will not say what the spring says. He says it is not for people, and then goes back to listen.

entries.title: Isolde Sings the Slow Songs
entries.text: The quick verses are gone. Isolde sings the slow ones carefully, so the next singer will have something left to take.

entries.title: Varo Watches the Held Snow
entries.text: Varo has sat on the rise for thirty winters. He knows the steppe by its sounds, and the Warden by the sound of its not making any.

entries.title: Hild Counts the Roofs
entries.text: Hild is elder of Hearn, and she told it plainly: the Shaped came at dusk with fire and took two people up the hill. She still speaks of it as this evening.

entries.title: Corin Mends What Is Left
entries.text: Corin has looked at every door in Hearn for a brother, Alder, and will tell anyone who asks which doors. It is how Corin says what cannot be said.

entries.title: Ebb Keeps the House
entries.text: Ebb says he was not brave, he was very scared. Everyone else says he was brave. Both are true, and he is learning that is allowed.

entries.title: Orm Reads the Shadows
entries.text: Orm's grandfather set the stones so that their shadows meet in the middle on the longest day. Orm has not missed one.

entries.title: Wyl Hung Rings on Nothing
entries.text: Wyl's rings hang over the Western Edge where the wind used to come up. He says the wind will use them when it comes back.

entries.title: Frost Binds Snow
entries.text: Packed snow goes to crust and holds a weight the snow would not. A lane of it is a lane that will still be there in an hour.

entries.title: A Gust Strips Snow
entries.text: The top of the drift goes to spindrift and is scoured to a ring. What was under it is harder than what was on top.

entries.title: Frost on Turf
entries.text: The blades stiffen and lie flat. No ice stays on grass; it is only a brittle white, gone by noon.

entries.title: Wind Lays the Grass
entries.text: A Gust leaves a lane where the blades are laid flat, and the grass stands up again by the hour. The meadow remembers wind a little while.

entries.title: Stone Lifts Snow and Earth
entries.text: A plate of the drift comes up with the ground under it, and what is thrown does not blow away: it falls and stays. Snow over stone remembers where it was taken from.

entries.title: Stone Tears the Turf
entries.text: The sod comes up whole, roots and all, and is thrown. The meadow will close the wound in a season; you can see the shape of it for a week.

entries.title: A Bloom Opens the Ground
entries.text: The ground opens like a flower and closes the same way: a bowl, a rim, and a slow rain of what was in it. Anything standing in the bowl stays there for a moment.

entries.title: An Updraft Lifts a Column
entries.text: Wind has a shape, and the shape can be stood on end. Whatever is over it rides it up: a handful of snow, a robe.

entries.title: Held Wind Becomes a Column
entries.text: Hold the Gust and it winds itself into a column. A column draws things in; a column stood still long enough, Maud says, is the shape the stones listen for.

entries.title: Frozen Things Break Whole
entries.text: A Shaped that has been frozen does not take a blow, it takes a breaking. That is the only way the cold is kind to anyone.

entries.title: Moving Warms the Robe
entries.text: Keep moving, chain one mode into the next, and the hem of the robe warms and the verbs reach further. Stand still and it forgets, in two breaths.

entries.title: Where the Snow Streams Off the Shelf
entries.text: Under the Shelf the restored wind turns upward and climbs the face. A robe opened there rises with no spell at all. It is the wind's, so it breathes: a gust lifts hard, and a lull lets you down.

entries.title: The Hill Is a Stair for the Wind
entries.text: The west wall of the manor hill sends the wind up it, and banners mark the places. Fly along the wall rather than at it, and the wind carries you above the crest.

entries.title: The Road of Two Winds
entries.text: The hill's wind and the lake ridge's wind make one road. A glider can cross Hearn, the lake and the Western Edge without touching the ground, if it banks its height on the hill first.

entries.title: A Gust With the Wind
entries.text: A Gust cast with the wind goes farther and carries what it meets. Cast against the wind it only stirs the dust. The chaff on a threshing floor knows the difference.
